title: Vitals grid shows a clipped sliver beside the names: on desktop when it opens, on a phone after a swipe to the end
evidence: From D2 (the phone fade after H79; first written as H102 on PR 1712, which was dropped; H102 is now PR 1714's). Desktop: at 1440 in real WebKit, with 13 saved weights, the vitals grid opens at scrollLeft 678 of 678: Trend is sticky at the right (styles.css .bt-timeline-scroll .bt-cell-trend), New 818-900, Trend 900-954. The left-most visible date column sits partly under the sticky name column, so only its "ys / dia" tail shows. H79 snaps whole columns only where Trend scrolls (widget-src/src/lib/useValuePage.ts:85-95). Phone: at 390, after a swipe to the end, a "lia" sliver (the tail of an older column's "sys / dia") shows beside the name column. H79's snap runs only when the grid is shown; a swipe ends at max scrollLeft (scrollWidth - clientWidth), which is not a whole column. Shot: d2-fade-390-end.png in session 701729d1's scratchpad. Remedy: on desktop, snap the left edge to a whole column with the sticky Trend's width taken out of max, so New stays clear of Trend; on a phone, make the scroll end on a whole column too. PR 1732 (closed, not merged) tried mandatory scroll-snap, a CSS round(up) range and a re-scroll on focusin. It did remove the sliver, but: (a) on desktop Chrome a mousedown focuses a saved-value button, and the re-scroll can move the cell away before mouseup, so the click is lost; (b) the rounded range leaves an empty band before Trend, 28 px at 390 in the default view and 60 px at 1440, and at 320 the end view shows no value; (c) without CSS round() support (Chrome below 125) the width declaration goes invalid at computed-value time and the sticky layout breaks. Proximity snap alone cannot fix the end, because max scroll is not on a column. Two ways forward: date-column widths that divide the data area exactly (this breaks width parity with the blood grid), or accept the sliver. Cosmetic. (H105)
